title: Annotatio IV §.VI open: Second century — Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus on the true Eucharistic sentence
pass_a_gloss: §. VI. Therefore in the age next receiving the Apostolic, i.e. the SECOND of the Christian era, the most excellent Martyrs of Christ openly enough professed the said true sentence concerning the Eucharist handed to them by Christ and the Apostles — IGNATIUS of Antioch at the beginning of this age; JUSTIN MARTYR in the middle; and also IRENÆUS, famous toward its end — professing Eucharistic truth so that the first turned the mind’s eyes to the chief part of the Eucharist to be held by faith alone; the second, lest that part be believed to be present alone, to the less principal, by no means to be transmuted into the chief; the Third finally to both, and to both presence and participation and the mode of presence and participation, of his own and of us all.
pass_b_english: §.VI: in the SECOND Christian age after the Apostolic, the leading martyrs openly professed the true Eucharistic sentence from Christ and the Apostles.

Ignatius (start) turns the mind to the chief part held by faith alone; Justin (middle) to the lesser part not to be turned into the chief; Irenaeus (end) to both — presence, participation, and their mode.
source_text: §. VI. Itaque SECULO Apostolicum proximè excipiente, i. e. Christianæ æræ SECUNDO, dictam de Eucharistia sententiam veram à Christo & Apostolis sibi traditam, apertè satis professi sunt Martyres Christi præstantissimi, IGNATIUS Antiochenus, Seculi hujus initiô; JUSTINUS MARTYR medio, nec non IRENÆUS, sub finem ejusdem celebres, ita verò veritatem Eucharisticam professi, ut primus ad præcipuam Eucharistiæ partem, fide sola tenendam; secundus, ne pars hæc adesse sola crederetur, ad minus principalem, in præcipuam neutiquam transmutandam; Tertius denique, ad utramque, nec non ad utriusq; cùm præsentiam ac participationem, tùm præsentiæ & participationis modum, & suæ, & nostrum omnium, Mentis oculos conversos voluerit.

choices.english: to be held by faith alone
